extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and students of philosophy/aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-theoretical guidance for analysing and writing poetry that distinguishes fancy and imagination, traces the law of association, and argues for the roles of will, judgment, and reason in poetic creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish fancy from imagination; deduce degree from kind
rubrics_metrics.description: My purpose to consider the influences of fancy and imagination as they are manifested in poetry, and from the different effects to conclude their diversity in kind; while it is my object to investigate the seminal principle, and then from the kind to deduce the degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'fancy' and 'imagination' as distinct faculties when analysing or producing poetry: first identify their kinds (species), then evaluate their degree (strength/extent). The author proposes to map branches (manifestations) and also to trace trunk and visible roots (underlying principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present an intelligible, perspicuous poetic theory
rubrics_metrics.description: I would gladly therefore spare both myself and others this labour, if I knew how without it to present an intelligible statement of my poetic creed,--not as my opinions, which weigh for nothing, but as deductions from established premises conveyed in such a form, as is calculated either to effect a fundamental conviction, or to receive a fundamental confutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defending a poetic theory or making critical claims, present clear deductions from established premises; anticipate 'complaints of obscurity' and aim for perspicuity so readers can either be convinced or confute the argument. Do not rely on mere conjecture or opponent's misreadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify inward experiences: passive, voluntary, spontaneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Our various sensations, perceptions, and movements were classed as active or passive, or as media partaking of both. A still finer distinction was soon established between the voluntary and the spontaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analysing mental operations relevant to poetry, distinguish whether an experience is passively received (receptive sense), actively willed, or spontaneous (a middle category). This classification affects how associations and creative acts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of association based on contemporaneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sir James Mackintosh ... affirmed in the Lectures ... that the law of association as established in the contemporaneity of the original impressions, formed the basis of all true psychology; and that any ontological or metaphysical science, not contained in such (that is, an empirical) psychology, was but a web of abstractions and generalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether associative links in a poem or mind are grounded chiefly in temporal contiguity of original impressions; the text debates this historical claim and suggests testing it by documents and argument rather than accepting it dogmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aristotle's general law of association (partial->total recall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas by having been together acquire a power of recalling each other; or every partial representation awakes the total representation of which it had been a part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the principle that fragments or parts in a work can evoke the whole complex impression they once formed; this underpins mechanical memory and passive fancy. Apply this when designing imagery or leitmotifs so parts summon broader associative fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aristotle's five occasioning causes of association
rubrics_metrics.description: In the practical determination of this common principle to particular recollections, he admits five agents or occasioning causes: first, connection in time, whether simultaneous, preceding, or successive; second, vicinity or connection in space; third, interdependence or necessary connection, as cause and effect; fourth, likeness; and fifth, contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating associative effects in poetry, rely deliberately on these five mechanisms (time, space, causal relation, likeness, contrast) to make images, phrases, or motifs recall one another; long 'leaps' of association may be explained by intermediate links that exhibit one or more of these relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish representations (ideas) from material motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle delivers a just theory without pretending to an hypothesis ... He uses indeed the word kinaeseis, to express what we call representations or ideas, but he carefully distinguishes them from material motion, designating the latter always by annexing the words en topo, or kata topon. On the contrary, in his treatise De Anima, he excludes place and motion from all the operations of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating imagery, ideas, or mental representations with physical motion or material processes when theorizing about poetic creation; treat mental operations as distinct from mechanical metaphors unless you explicitly adopt a materialist model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware reducing association to mechanical vibrations or time-alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus the principle of contemporaneity, which Aristotle had made the common condition of all the laws of association, Hartley was constrained to represent as being itself the sole law. ... Had this been really the case, the consequence would have been, that our whole life would be divided between the despotism of outward impressions, and that of senseless and passive memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not explain poetic creativity or mental life as merely the propagation of material vibrations or as governed solely by temporal contiguity; such reductionism erases agency (will, reason, judgment) and leads to absurd moral and aesthetic consequences. Preserve the role of active faculties in shaping art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of choice and judgment in shaping association into memory or fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: It remains then for me, first to state wherein Hartley differs from Aristotle; then, to exhibit the grounds of my conviction, that he differed only to err: and next as the result, to show, by what influences of the choice and judgment the associative power becomes either memory or fancy; and, in conclusion, to appropriate the remaining offices of the mind to the reason, and the imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating or assessing poetic effects, account for how deliberate choice and critical judgment transform raw associative impulses into either remembered content or into 'fancy' (free imaginative elaboration). Assign distinct functions to reason and imagination in the creative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent impressions persist and may reproduce in original order
rubrics_metrics.description: This authenticated case furnishes both proof and instance, that reliques of sensation may exist for an indefinite time in a latent state, in the very same order in which they were originally impressed; and as we cannot rationally suppose the feverish state of the brain to act in any other way than as a stimulus, this fact ... contributes to make it even probable, that all thoughts are in themselves imperishable;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the idea that impressions can lie latent and later re-emerge in their original sequence as a device in poetry or narrative: recollection, dream-states, or fevered speech can legitimately source language and imagery that appear spontaneously but have a traceable origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve moral and intellectual agency against mechanistic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: According to this system, it is not the affections and passions that are at work ... We only fancy, that we act from rational resolves, or prudent motives, or from impulses of anger, love, or generosity. ... The existence of an infinite spirit, of an intelligent and holy will, must, on this system, be mere articulated motions of the air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In both criticism and creative practice, resist theories that nullify agency and moral responsibility by treating human thought and action as mere mechanical by-products. Artistic accounts should allow for genuine affections, motives, and ethical dimensions rather than reducing them to epiphenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical and documentary evidence when attributing theoretical priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The latter clause involves for the greater part a mere question of fact and history, and the accuracy of the statement is to be tried by documents rather than reasoning. First, then, I deny Hobbes’s claim in toto: for he had been anticipated by Des Cartes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming that a psychological or aesthetic principle originated with a particular thinker, verify priority with historical documents and texts. Critical evaluations of theoretical claims should be grounded in textual-historical evidence as well as argument.
